Valley Fever forecasts for California counties

Counties ranked by total cases with the best model and average error for each feature set

Log scale. Yes, the models predict on a log scale. The target is the month-to-month change in log(1 + cases per 100,000). Forecasts are converted back to cases per 100,000 for the charts and the rate errors, and each forecast starts from the last observed month.

How to read the errors. RMSE and MAE are averaged over every forecast month in every rolling window, on that log-change scale. Smaller is better. Each section's summary line also gives the error in cases per 100,000. "vs seasonal naive" and "vs no change" show how much lower a model's RMSE is than each baseline at the same horizon. Seasonal naive repeats last year's change. No change repeats last month's value, which is the stricter test. Baselines are shown for comparison and are never picked as the best model.

Which model the charts show. Each chart opens with the best model for that county and feature set, chosen by RMSE averaged over the 1, 3 and 6 month horizons, plus the no-change baseline. The best model stays the same when you change the horizon, so at a single horizon another model can score slightly better. Models you turn on or off are kept while you change the horizon and reset when you change county.

Feature sets. Environment uses weather, air quality, fire and pesticide data. Media uses California-wide article and tweet measures, so every county sees the same media signal. Media + environment uses both. All three include the county's recent case changes. Feature importance is averaged over every fitted window of the best model that reports it (Ridge, Random forest, XGBoost or SARIMAX). SARIMAX importance covers only its five chosen outside predictors, because it models past cases itself. If the LSTM is best, the importance comes from the best of the other four models. Findings are predictive and associational, not causal.
